newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday, with the active A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen boosting most of the repo rates, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract advanced to 6.00 percent from 2.50 percent last Friday.
Turnover increased to 11.61 million lots from 7.07 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The repo rates have been pushed up by bigger demand for money from some institutions due to a more active A share market today and a new listing and a new issue tomorrow," one trader said.
The Shanghai Minfeng Holding Co. Ltd will issue shares on the Shanghai stock market while Eastern Communications will list its new A shares.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed with sentiment still weak.
The nine contracts performed in different directions with six up and three down.
The most active 7-year bond that matures in Nov 2003 moved down to 98.70 yuan from 99.07 yuan last Friday.
The turnover of this bond fell sharply to 0.41 billion yuan from 1.15 billion yuan.
The combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 957,014 lots from 1.69 million lots.
"The fact that the new bond fell below the issuing price on its first trading day has dampened the market sentiment, and there is no signs of recovery," said one trader.
"After Friday's rally, some investors were eager to sell for cash, which led to the seven-year bond falling further today," said another trader.
